Map one location surface

Source: R/surface_methods.R
plot.loc_surface.Rd

Draws the probability surface of one animal and bin on its grid, with its credible regions outlined and the receivers listening in the bin marked.

Usage

# S3 method for loc_surface
plot(x, animal_id = NULL, bin_start = NULL, level = c(0.5, 0.95), ...)

Arguments

x

A location surface from location_surface().

animal_id

The animal to draw; the first in the surface by default.

bin_start

Start of the bin to draw (POSIXct, or text read as UTC); the animal's first bin by default.

level

One or two levels of the credible regions outlined, each above 0 and at most 1, or NULL for none. The default draws the 50% and 95% regions.

...

ext, the extent to draw, as a terra::ext() or as c(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax). Other arguments are ignored with a warning; change the figure by adding ggplot2 layers, scales or ggplot2::labs() to the plot it returns. On a grid in metres the axes are titled "Easting (m)" and "Northing (m)", with the grid's coordinate reference system named in the brackets when the grid carries one: "UTM 17N" for a UTM zone, otherwise its authority code, such as "EPSG:3161".

Value

A ggplot object. It prints when not assigned; assign it to add layers, such as a track with ggplot2::geom_path(), or to save it with ggplot2::ggsave().

Details

The surface is drawn with scale_fill_probability(), the magma scale of every positionR probability map, over the stored cells. The scale runs from 0 to the largest probability of a cell in the bin, which is the top label of the key, because each cell holds a small share of the animal's position and on 0 to 1 the whole map would be black. Other water cells are grey and land is blank. The title names the animal and the start of the bin on one line above the map and its keys. Each credible region is drawn as one outline of its cells, in a colour outside the magma scale over a thin dark line so it reads on the bright and the dark ends of the scale: with two levels, the smaller (by default 50%) is sky blue and the larger (95%) bluish green; one level is drawn bluish green. The key is titled "Credible region". When the larger region spans under a tenth of the map's longer side, both rings are drawn at half width, so the cells inside a small region still show. The receivers listening in the bin are drawn over the regions by layer_receivers(), the receiver mark of every positionR map: a ring over a dark ring one step wider, never filled, so the surface shows through. A receiver that detected the animal is a yellow ring whose area is proportional to its count, from zero, up to 6 mm across at the largest count of the bin; the key "Detections" shows at most three counts. A receiver that heard none is a white ring, keyed "No detections". Only the receivers inside the map are drawn and keyed, so a key never names a mark the map does not show.

The map zooms to the stored cells and the receivers that detected the animal, a quarter wider on each side; silent receivers near that box (within its longer side) widen it, so the map shows where the animal was not heard without zooming out to a whole array. On a grid in metres each side of the map is at least 1.5 km and at least three quarters of the longer side. Give ext to draw another extent. The figure is built with ggplot2 and theme_positionr(), with equal coordinates and a scale bar.

Examples

tif <- system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif", package = "detfield")
grid <- terra::rast(tif)
# Beyond 2 km the Stoney curve is below 0.001 at every receiver; leaving
# those pairs out keeps the example quick.
dist <- water_distances(grid, stoney_track$receivers,
                        max_distance = 2000)
model <- de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500), depth = c(1, 35))
field <- de_field(dist, de_model(model, sigma = list(station_hour = 0)))
#> 194 of 7,669 receiver-cell pairs with p >= 0.05 have land on the
#>   straight line between them; with blocked = 0 the curve is read on
#>   them as if the line were clear. See `blocked` in ?de_model.
# Position one animal in one hour, the hour the map draws
dets <- subset(stoney_track$detections, animal_id == "stoney-01" &
                 format(datetime, "%d %H", tz = "UTC") == "01 07")
counts <- bin_detections(dets, stoney_track$receivers, stoney_track$tags)
surface <- location_surface(counts, field)
plot(surface)

plot(surface, level = 0.95)
